app.title: Rainfall Verification Dashboard
app.summary: The person points the sidebar at a folder of gridded forecast files and an observation file, picks one or more models, lead times, a rain threshold and a single day or a seasonal date range, then draws a box on the observed map (or types its bounds) and presses Run. Each forecast is regridded onto the observation grid, and the dashboard shows observed and forecast maps, box-mean rainfall against valid date, and a table of categorical and continuous scores per model and lead, plotted against lead time with optional bootstrap confidence intervals. Further panels give per-grid-cell score maps, a Taylor diagram and Q–Q plot, neighbourhood and displacement diagnostics, and probabilistic diagnostics for ensembles. The score tables download as CSV and every figure exports as an image.

task.text: Score gridded forecasts against gridded observations over a chosen region, threshold and period, so models and lead times can be compared on matched samples.

data.text: Gridded daily fields on a latitude-longitude grid: one observation file with a time axis, and forecast files per model and lead time, either deterministic or with ensemble members stored as separate variables, in NetCDF or GRIB2.
data.item: a forecast field for one model, lead time and valid date, paired with the observed field for that date

stage.text: verifying model forecasts against observations after the forecasts are archived, before writing them up

mechanism.text: The sidebar sets the files, models, leads, threshold, period and options, and nothing is recomputed until Run is pressed. A box drawn on the observed heatmap, kept in sync with numeric bounds, sets the scoring region and is drawn as a rectangle on every map panel. Results then appear in a stack of panels: forecast maps with shared zoom and pan, a score table, score-versus-lead plots with confidence bars, score maps per cell, and diagnostic plots, each with a CSV or figure export.

field.text: forecast verification of gridded precipitation in meteorology

workflow.name: score model outputs against observations and compare models

steps.here: type a models base directory and an observation file path; models are found as sub-folders or filename prefixes, lead times are read from dayN tokens in filenames, and units are read from file attributes or set by hand

steps.step: choose which models, conditions and period to score
steps.here: pick a single model or several to compare, the lead times, ensemble mean or probabilistic verification, a rain threshold in mm, matched samples only, and a Daily date or a Seasonal date-range slider
drag a box on the observed rainfall map or type lon/lat bounds; the box is drawn in red on every map and applied when Run is pressed

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Run regrids each forecast bilinearly onto the observation grid, sums contingency counts and running sums over the box and dates, and computes POD/FAR/CSI/BIAS/ETS/HSS and extremal scores, ME/MAE/RMSE/CORR, or Brier/BSS/CRPS, with optional date-resampling bootstrap CIs
forecast maps in a model × lead grid with shared zoom and pan, box-mean rainfall against valid date per model, scores plotted against lead with one line per model, and a Taylor diagram and Q–Q plot

steps.step: see where in space the result holds
steps.here: per-grid-cell maps of a chosen continuous, categorical or probabilistic score for each model and lead; FSS against neighbourhood width and a CRA displacement/volume/pattern breakdown; reliability, ROC, economic value, PIT and spread–skill for ensembles
score and CRA tables download as CSV, every figure exports as PNG/JPEG/SVG/PDF, and each run is appended to an audit log

distinctive: forecasts on any grid are bilinearly regridded onto the observation grid before scoring, so models with different resolutions are scored on the same cells
a matched-samples option scores every model only on the valid dates all models and the observations share, so the comparison across models is fair
scores are pooled from summed contingency counts and running sums over dates rather than averaged daily, and the bootstrap resamples whole dates so spatial correlation within a day is kept
an event is defined by one rain threshold applied as ≥ to both fields, and the same threshold drives the categorical scores, FSS and the event probabilities for Brier score
nothing recomputes while settings change; one Run button triggers the whole computation, so large gridded archives are read one time-slice at a time
